To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have investigated two practical receiver architectures for the non-regenarative MIMO-OFDF relay system.
the performances of PSR and TSR are greatly affected by both the relay position and the number of antennas at the relay.

(1) the performance of the proposed TSR is greatly affected by the position of the relay; (2) the achievable information rate of TSR decreases when the relay is located in the middle of source and destination; (3) PSR always out-performs TSR; and (4) the number of antennas has a more significant influence than the number of sub-carriers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical MIMO-OFDN relaying systems, and the proposed protocols and algorithms are of great importance for the future wireless communication systems.
the performance of the MIMO-OFDMA relaying system, where the relay node can simultaneously transfer information to the destination and harvest energy from the source.
the fundamental performance limits for two practical protocols in the MIMO-OFDN relay networks, which provides useful insights for the system design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relay position, the number of antennas, the number of subcarrier, and the CSI are all important factors to affect the system performance of the MIMO-OFD relaying system.
the relay position is the most important factor affecting the system performance in the considered MIMO-OFDFM relaying system.
TSR is better than PSR when the relay is close to either the source or the destination, but PSR is always superior to TSR when the relay is far from both the source and destination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a novel protocol to achieve the simultaneous wireless information transmission and energy transfer in MIMO-OFD relay networks, which can be regarded as an important supplement to the existing work on this topic.
the proposed protocols can achieve the optimal information rate with full CSI and that PSR is more energy efficient and robust than TSR.

the relay position is a critical parameter that should be carefully considered in the design of wireless powered relaying systems, and the PSR protocol is more suitable for MIMO-OFDMA relaying systems than TSR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed protocols can be used in the design of wireless information and energy harvesting MIMO-OFDMA networks.
the proposed protocols can achieve a significant performance gain compared with conventional relaying schemes.
the performance of TSR can be improved by increasing the number of antennas at the relay, but the performance of PSR is not affected by the number of antennas.
